subject: Behavioral Economics
title: Transparency in Nudging
description: A 60-second lesson on Transparency in Nudging.

hook.text: Should governments disclose that they use nudges? A survey found 86% of people support nudges, but only when told about.

buildup.text: Transparency means telling citizens that behavioral techniques are being used.

discovery.text: Loewenstein found that disclosed nudges are nearly as effective as secret ones. Transparency doesn't destroy the effect.

twist.text: Some nudges lose power when disclosed. If you know a countdown timer is fake, it stops working.

climax.text: Transparency is a test: if a nudge still works when people know about it, it's legitimate.

punchline.text: If the nudge survives disclosure, it deserves to stay.

quiz.question: Why is the 'transparency test' useful for evaluating nudges?
options: All nudges fail when disclosed, so the test identifies them
If a nudge works after disclosure, it is legitimate; if it fails, it was manipulation

details.summary: Transparency in nudging means disclosing to citizens that behavioral interventions are being used. Research shows that transparent nudges maintain most of their effectiveness while increasing public trust and ethical legitimacy of the intervention.
details.whyItMatters: If nudges only work when people do not know about them, their ethical foundation is weak. The finding that transparent nudges remain effective strengthens the case for behavioral policy by showing it respects informed consent.
takeaways: Transparent nudges retain most of their effectiveness when disclosed
Disclosure increases public trust in government behavioral interventions
Transparency strengthens the ethical legitimacy of nudge-based policies

faq.question: Do nudges stop working once people know about them?
faq.answer: Mostly not. Studies show that disclosing a default nudge reduces its effect by only 2 to 5 percentage points from a base of 30 to 50 points. The convenience and inertia that make defaults powerful persist even when the nudge is transparent.

faq.question: Should all government nudges be disclosed to citizens?
faq.answer: Most behavioral policy experts say yes. Transparency builds trust, respects autonomy, and maintains democratic accountability. The small loss in effectiveness is outweighed by the gain in legitimacy and public support.
